purpose: Provider-free proof that durable Content Factory restart reuses unchanged work and invalidates only semantically dependent worker executions rather than treating Git implementation-head identity as a universal invalidation key.

scenarios.expectation: A Git-head-only change with identical worker inputs and dependency contracts reuses all completed worker executions without provider calls.
A Practice compiler contract change invalidates Practice and assurance dependants while retaining Course Knowledge Model, Learn and independent assessment-generation work.
An Assessment Blueprint compiler contract change invalidates the assessment branch and assurance dependants without invalidating Learn or Practice.

A Coverage contract change invalidates Course Knowledge Model and all genuinely coverage-dependent learning, assessment and assurance work while preserving unrelated identity, source discovery, structured evidence and Board Alignment work.
Cross-head reuse preserves original retry and usage-cost provenance and the cumulative course spend ledger does not double-charge reused work.
A changed-head resume replays the current pipeline from requested while the semantic worker cache supplies only dependency-compatible prior executions.

evidence: docs/technical/Content Factory Durable Resume and Spend.md

compatibility.rule: Legacy schema-v1 worker cache entries remain same-head-only. A same-head reuse can migrate them into semantic schema-v2 cache records; cross-head reuse requires a schema-v2 dependency fingerprint.

limitations: Q5 proves restart, reuse, invalidation and provenance mechanics; it does not prove educational correctness.
Legacy schema-v1 cache entries are deliberately not inferred safe across a head change and may require one regeneration before semantic reuse is available.
Q6 repeated qualification stability remains required before overall reliability qualification can change.
Overall reliability qualification remains paused and paid live-pilot eligibility remains false.
